description:
Elevation view (left): A square sign face with a dashed diamond outline inside it (representing a diamond sign shape on a square panel) is mounted on a perforated square-tube post. Blind rivets are shown at the top and bottom corners of the diamond and a center blind rivet at the middle. A callout reads 'Center blind rivet used on 36" or large signs'. A callout reads 'Max. 10 sq ft sign area. For larger signs see Standard Plan S-476.1'. The sign's left edge is dimensioned 18" from a vertical reference line at the curb face. The bottom of the sign is dimensioned 7' minimum over the pedestrian area (see Note 3) down to the sidewalk surface. A second horizontal dimension from the curb-face reference line to the post reads 24" min. (see Note 1). The post has a break line, continues down through the sidewalk, and a dimension of 6" to 8" marks the insertion depth of the post into the anchor assembly below the sidewalk surface. A bracket labeled 'See Detail' covers the post and anchor below grade. The sidewalk and curb are drawn in section at the bottom with the curb on the left.

Detail (right, isometric): A perforated square-tube post 2" x 2" is inserted 6" to 8" deep into the anchor assembly (callout 'Insert 2" X 2" post 6" to 8" deep into the anchor assembly'). A sleeve labeled 2 1/2" X 2 1/2" X 18" sits at the sidewalk surface with 2 blind rivets through it ('2 Blind rivets') and '2 holes above surface' labeled at the sleeve top, with a 'See Note 2' reference at the sleeve. Below the sleeve the anchor, labeled 2 1/4" X 2 1/4" X 30", extends down through the concrete sidewalk. The sidewalk slab is shown as a stippled concrete section with the curb at left.
notes:
Note (general):
1. 30" typical for parking signs. 36" typical for warning and regulatory signs. (This is the value of the 24" minimum dimension marked 'see Note 1' on the elevation, measured from the curb face reference line to the post.)
2. Posts for parking signs to be installed at 45 degree angle to curb. Posts for warning and regulatory signs to be installed at 90 degree angle to curb.
3. 9'6" minimum for street name signs, 7'6" typical for parking signs, 4' typical for W31(CA), W1-6 and W1-7, 4' typical to top of sign for W1-8, W12-1, OM1-3 and OM4-3. (These are mounting heights that apply in place of the 7' minimum over the pedestrian area, as referenced on the elevation.)

Callouts: Blind rivet (top and bottom). Center blind rivet used on 36" or larger signs. Max. 10 sq ft sign area. For larger signs see Standard Plan S-476.1. 18" (sign to curb reference line). 7' min. over pedestrian area (see Note 3). 24" min. (see Note 1). 6" to 8" insertion depth. See Detail. Insert 2" x 2" post 6" to 8" deep into the anchor assembly. 2 blind rivets. 2 holes above surface. See Note 2. Sleeve 2 1/2" x 2 1/2" x 18". Anchor 2 1/4" x 2 1/4" x 30".
title: Sign Post Installation
summary: Shows installation of a perforated square-tube sign post set in an anchor sleeve in the sidewalk, for signs up to 10 sq ft. The 2 in. x 2 in. post is inserted 6 in. to 8 in. into the anchor assembly and secured with two blind rivets, with a 2 1/2 in. x 2 1/2 in. x 18 in. sleeve over a 2 1/4 in. x 2 1/4 in. x 30 in. anchor. The sign is set 18 in. from the curb face with 7 ft minimum clearance over pedestrian areas, and parking signs are set at 45 degrees to the curb while warning and regulatory signs are set at 90 degrees. Larger signs use S-476.1.

description:
Signs to 10 sq. ft.: Elevation of a steel street light pole with a mast arm and luminaire at the top, set in a sidewalk with curb at left. A rounded-rectangle sign with three dashed stiffener channels is centered on the pole ('Center sign on pole'), with its bottom dimensioned 15' above the sidewalk. Callout: for signs 42" and longer secure to street light with heavy duty 2-bolt "D" clip in each stiffener channel.

Signs 10 to 18 sq. ft.: Elevation of a single post carrying a sign with three dashed horizontal stiffener channels, secured to the post with a square head bolt in each stiffener channel. The sign is set back 18" from the curb face, the post is 2' from the sign's left edge, and the sign is 6' maximum wide. The bottom of the sign is 7' above the sidewalk. The post is 4' minimum from the property line, which is drawn as a dash-dot vertical line at right. The post is marked 'See Note 1' at the sidewalk.

Signs 18 to 32 sq. ft.: Elevation of a sign with four dashed stiffener channels mounted on two posts, each secured with a square head bolt in each stiffener channel. The sign is set back 18" from the curb face, the bottom is 7' above the sidewalk, the two posts are 4' minimum apart, and the property line is at right. Both posts are marked 'See Note 1'.

Detail: Section through the post base. A 2 1/2" x 2 1/2" x 14', 10 gauge post is inserted 6" to 8" into the anchor ('Insert post 6"~8" into the anchor'). The anchor base is 3" x 3" x 30", 7 gauge, non-perforated, with 2 drilled holes at the top, and its top sits at the sidewalk surface with the stippled concrete shown beside it.
notes:
1. See Detail for square tube sign post installation.
2. Sign stiffener system and hardware per standard plan S-476.0.
3. Signs greater than 32 sq. ft. should be placed on a cantilever standard.
4. Sign may not extend beyond property line.
5. Large roadside mountings on electroliers are permitted only when the poles are steel and embedded in concrete sidewalks.

View callouts: Signs to 10 sq. ft.: center sign on pole, 15' above the sidewalk. For signs 42" and longer, secure to street light with heavy duty 2-bolt "D" clip in each stiffener channel. Signs 10 to 18 sq. ft. and 18 to 32 sq. ft.: secure to post with square head bolt in each stiffener channel. Detail: 2 1/2" x 2 1/2" x 14', 10 gauge post. Insert post 6" to 8" into the anchor. 3" x 3" x 30", 7 gauge non-perforated anchor base (2 drilled holes at the top).
title: Posting Detail for Large Roadside Signs
summary: Shows mounting of large roadside signs by area: signs to 10 sq ft on a street light pole centered 15 ft above the sidewalk, signs 10 to 18 sq ft on one post, and signs 18 to 32 sq ft on two posts 4 ft minimum apart. Signs are set 18 in. back from the curb with 7 ft bottom clearance and 4 ft minimum from the property line. Posts are 2 1/2 in. x 2 1/2 in. x 14 ft, 10 gauge, set in a 3 in. x 3 in. x 30 in. 7 gauge anchor base. Signs over 32 sq ft go on a cantilever standard.

description:
Plan view, upper left (crosswalk at an intersection corner pair): A ladder (continental) crosswalk crosses the roadway with 2' wide bars, with optional RPMs (raised pavement markers) shown as small squares on each side of the bars ('RPM's Optional', see Note 6). A crosswalk sign assembly post is shown at each curb. Sign options shown above the crosswalk: W11-15 (bicycle and pedestrian) or W11-2 (pedestrian) diamond signs, each with a W16-7p diagonal arrow plate, or the S1-1 school sign with a W16-7p plate ('School Crosswalk Warning Assembly B (CA code)'). Each assembly is labeled 'CROSSWALK SIGN ASSEMBLY'. R1-5 'Optional' (see Note 7) YIELD HERE TO PEDESTRIANS signs sit upstream of the crosswalk with yield line triangles ('Yield Line "Optional" (See Note 7 & See Fig 3B-17(CA), CA MUTCD)'). A 20' - 50' per CA MUTCD dimension is shown from the crosswalk to the yield line. Lower left shows the R1-5 and R1-5a MOD (YIELD HERE TO bicycle and pedestrian) sign faces, both 'Optional' (see Note 7), separated by '-OR-'.

Plan view, middle (advance signing and markings on a two-way street): Two approaches are shown, each with the crosswalk at one end and advance signing at distance C. Dimension C ** runs from the crosswalk to the advance sign W11-15, W11-2, or Assembly D (CA). Advance pavement markings read 'PED XING' (with asterisk, or 'SLOW SCHOOL XING' or 'SCHOOL XING') and are placed with 8', 32', 8' spacing between the two marking sets. A parked vehicle width of 8' and the curb lane width W are dimensioned. School Crosswalk Warning Assembly D (CA code) is shown with the S1-1 school sign above a W16-9p AHEAD plate. Yield lines and R1-5 'Optional' signs are shown at the crosswalk approach.

Detail, lower right: A crosswalk ladder with 2' bars centered on DYCL (double yellow centerline) and lane lines, with RPMs at each bar. Callout: 'Install markings along striping and space at 4 1/2', 5', 5 1/2' and 6' C-C for 9', 10', 11' and 12' lanes, respectively. 2' white or yellow, centered on DYCL and lane lines.'

Table (advance warning sign placement C):
Posted speed (mph) / C (ft)
25 / 100
30 / 100
35 / 125
40 / 175
Legend: * or "SLOW SCHOOL XING" or "SCHOOL XING". ** Dimension of field installation of signs or markings may exceed the figures in the table by up to 100 feet per work order or plan in order to adjust to field conditions. C = Advance warning sign placement (CA MUTCD, Table 2C-4 and Part 2).
notes:
1. Implementation. This standard plan applies to new installations and reinstallations of marked crosswalks and to marked crosswalks determined to be retained as a result of a study on multi-lane facilities. Use of signs shall be in coordination with all other controls shown on this plan.
2. Sign posting at crosswalk. Crosswalk Sign Assembly signs shall be posted and should be positioned within ten feet of the crosswalk. These signs generally shall be posted back-to-back so that one sign is on the right and the other on the left. If a raised median with a width of 6' or greater exists, the left sign shall be in the median. These signs should be 36" x 36". The W16-9p or W16-7p plates shall be 36" wide. All signs shall be fluorescent yellow-green.
3. Advance sign posting. Advance Pedestrian Crossing W11-15, W11-2 signs, or Assembly D (CA) signs shall be posted as shown and shall be fluorescent yellow-green. R1-5 signs shall be posted and positioned within ten feet of the yield limit line. These locations may be adjusted to accommodate field conditions. All signs should be 36" x 36".
4. Pavement markings. "PED XING" or "SCHOOL XING" pavement markings shall be installed as shown except the yellow "SLOW SCHOOL XING" pavement markings shall be installed in advance of uncontrolled yellow school crosswalks. If the crosswalk spacing is less than 500 feet, only one set of pavement markings is required in advance of the first crosswalk.
5. Midblock crosswalks. This standard plan also applies at uncontrolled approaches to midblock crosswalks.
6. Raised pavement markings (RPM). Install RPMs one each side of crosswalk bar facing approach lanes. Two-way clear (white) or two-way amber (yellow) per CALTRANS standards and specifications may be installed corresponding to the crosswalk color.
7. R1-5 (YIELD HERE TO PEDESTRIANS) signs and yield lines. For uncontrolled locations with more than one lane in each direction of travel, advance yield lines may be used. Yield lines shall be supplemented with R1-5 signs.

Legend and table notes: * or "SLOW SCHOOL XING" or "SCHOOL XING". ** Dimension of field installation of signs or markings may exceed the figures in the table by up to 100 feet per work order or plan in order to adjust to field conditions. C = Advance warning sign placement (CA MUTCD, Table 2C-4 and Part 2).
title: Traffic Controls for Marked Crosswalks on Uncontrolled Approaches (Sheet 1 of 4)
summary: Sheet 1 of 4 of the standard plan for signing and markings at marked crosswalks on uncontrolled approaches. It shows crosswalk sign assemblies with W11-2 or W11-15 and W16-7p plates or S1-1 school signs, advance warning signs at distance C (100 ft to 175 ft by speed), optional R1-5 yield-here-to-pedestrians signs with yield lines, PED XING or SCHOOL XING pavement markings, and optional RPMs. Seven notes cover implementation, sign posting, markings, midblock crosswalks, RPMs and yield lines.

description:
Plan view, upper (one direction of travel): Part of an arterial with a curb lane of width W next to the curb, an 8' wide parked vehicle shown in the parking lane, and a ladder crosswalk at the left end beside a curb return. A pedestrian is shown at the crosswalk edge 4' into the roadway from the curb line. A motorist vehicle approaching from the right is shown with a sight line to the pedestrian, with the driver assumed 3' from the lane line. Red curb of length A runs along the curb starting at the crosswalk end and extending upstream, and a 50' min. dimension 'Per MPP Sec. 342' is shown over the same stretch. Dimension A is measured from the side street curb line prolongation to the upstream end of the red curb. Dimension B (safe stopping distance) runs from the pedestrian to the driver position. Yield line triangles cross the approach lanes at the crosswalk, post markers show sign locations, and advance 'PED XING' pavement markings with an asterisk are shown upstream.

Plan view, lower (opposite direction and opposite curb): The same layout mirrored, with the crosswalk on the right, the red curb on the lower curb, the vehicle on the left, and the 3', W, 8', 4', A, B and 50' min. dimensions repeated.

Table (calculated A distances, ft), top left. Columns are posted speed 25, 30, 35, 40 mph, rows are curb lane width W (ft):
W = 18: 56, 71, 88, 107
W = 19: 51, 65, 81, 98
W = 20: 47, 60, 74, 90
W = 21: 44, 56, 69, 84
W = 22: 41, 52, 65, 78
W = 23: 38, 49, 61, 74
W = 24: 36, 46, 57, 69

Table (B), top right. Posted speed (mph) / B (ft): 25 / 153, 30 / 195, 35 / 242, 40 / 294.

Formulas and definitions are in the text block at the top of the sheet (see Notes).
notes:
A = 4B / (W-7) = curb stopping prohibition necessary for motorist to see a pedestrian at a point 4' into the roadway. LADOT practice is to install 50 feet of red curb on arterial approaches to side streets, measured from the side street curb line prolongation. Install this minimum dimension whenever the calculated A distance results in a lesser dimension. (See Note 1.)
B = Safe stopping distance = 1.47 VT + 1.075 V^2/a
V = Posted speed + 5 mph (chart listings calculated on posted speed + 5 mph)
T = Perception-reaction time of 1.5 seconds (driver previously alerted with advance sign and pavement markings)
a = Deceleration rate = 11.2 ft/s^2 (AASHTO Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, Stopping Sight Distance; printed on the sheet as ASSHTO in the formula line)
W = Curb lane width (driver is assumed to be 3' from lane line)

Notes:
1. One-way streets. Because one-way streets place drivers closer to the curb on the left side of the roadway, use A = 4B/(W-11) for left side pedestrian approach. This distance is not shown above.
2. Signs. See Sheet 1 for appropriate signs.
title: Red Curb for Sight Distance to Pedestrian Crossings (S-481.0, Sheet 2 of 4)
summary: Sheet 2 of 4 gives the red curb length A needed so a motorist can see a pedestrian standing 4 ft into the roadway, using A = 4B/(W-7). A table lists A for curb lane widths of 18 ft to 24 ft at 25 to 40 mph, for example 56 ft to 107 ft at 18 ft width, and B is 153, 195, 242 and 294 ft. LADOT practice sets a 50 ft minimum red curb on arterial approaches per MPP Sec. 342. One-way streets use A = 4B/(W-11) on the left side.

description:
Plan view, upper (one direction): An arterial approach with a curb extension at the crosswalk. A pedestrian stands at the curbline of the curb extension next to a ladder crosswalk at the left. The curb extension is 7' wide (dimension 7') compared with the 8' wide parking lane (dimension 8' shown at the parked vehicle). Red curb of length A runs along the curb, starting at the crosswalk end and following the curb extension taper out to the full curb line. The driver is shown at distance B from the pedestrian with a sight line to the pedestrian, 3' from the lane line, in a lane of width W. Yield line triangles cross the approach lanes. Advance 'PED XING' pavement markings with an asterisk are shown upstream. Curb ramps are drawn at the curb extension and at the opposite corner.

Plan view, lower (opposite direction): Mirrored layout with the crosswalk on the right, the red curb on the lower curb, a 50' min. dimension 'Per MPP Sec. 342', dimensions A and B, and a pedestrian at the curbline of the curb extension.

Table (calculated A distances, ft), top left. Columns are posted speed 25, 30, 35, 40 mph, rows are curb lane width W (ft):
W = 18: 19, 24, 30, 37
W = 19: 17, 22, 27, 33
W = 20: 15, 20, 24, 29
W = 21: 14, 18, 22, 27
W = 22: 13, 16, 20, 25
W = 23: 12, 15, 19, 23
W = 24: 11, 14, 17, 21

Table (B), top right. Posted speed (mph) / B (ft): 25 / 153, 30 / 195, 35 / 242, 40 / 294.
notes:
A = B/(W-10) = Curb stopping prohibition necessary for a motorist to see a pedestrian at the curbline of the curb extension. This formula assumes that the curb extension is 7' wide compared to the 8' wide parking lane.

Notes:
1. Signs. See Sheet 1 for appropriate signs.

Dimension callouts: 50' min. Per MPP Sec. 342 (red curb minimum where the calculated A is less).
title: Red Curb for Sight Distance to Pedestrian Crossings with Curb Extension (S-481.0, Sheet 3 of 4)
summary: Sheet 3 of 4 gives the red curb length A where a curb extension is present, using A = B/(W-10), which assumes a 7 ft wide curb extension against an 8 ft parking lane. A table lists A for curb lane widths of 18 ft to 24 ft at 25 to 40 mph, from 11 ft to 37 ft, with B of 153, 195, 242 and 294 ft. A 50 ft minimum red curb per MPP Sec. 342 applies where the calculated A is less.

description:
Plan view: A typical intersection with a main two-lane street running left to right and a ladder crosswalk across it at the center, with RPMs (raised pavement markers) shown optionally beside each crosswalk bar ('RPM's "Optional"', see Note 6, Sheet 1). The centerline is widened on each approach into a pair of lines forming a narrow median, with 2' typical width between the lines, and tapers of Min. 30' at the start of each widening ('Min. 30' TAPERS'). Yield line triangles are shown across the approach lanes before the crosswalk, and post markers show sign locations.
Left approach: the widened centerline ends at a stub near the crosswalk with a Min. 20' dimension for the widened portion. 'INSTALL 100' OF 4" DOUBLE WHITE LINE' is called out along the lane edge. An R1-6 PADDLE SIGN "Optional" is placed at the end of the widening.
Right approach: the widened centerline extends Min. 35' from the crosswalk before the Min. 30' tapers. 'INSTALL 100' OF DOUBLE WHITE LINE' is called out beside the lane. A 20'-50' dimension locates the R1-6 paddle sign (optional) from the crosswalk or yield line.
notes:
1. Signs. See Sheet 1 for appropriate signs.

Callouts: Min. 20'. Min. 35'. Min. 30' tapers. 2' typ. 20'-50'. Install 100' of 4" double white line (left approach). Install 100' of double white line (right approach). R1-6 paddle sign "Optional". RPMs "Optional" (see Note 6, Sheet 1).
title: Centerline Widening (Typical) at Intersections (S-481.0, Sheet 4 of 4)
summary: Sheet 4 of 4 shows typical centerline widening at an intersection with a marked crosswalk. The centerline is split into a 2 ft wide double line with minimum 30 ft tapers, with minimum 20 ft and 35 ft widened lengths on the two approaches and 100 ft of double white line installed. An optional R1-6 paddle sign is placed 20 ft to 50 ft from the crosswalk and RPMs are optional.

description:
Plan view, left: A segment of a street with a break line in the middle, showing a continental (ladder) crosswalk at the left end with 2' white or yellow bars centered on the DYCL (double yellow centerline) and lane lines, an S symbol (signal) in the crosswalk, and curb ramps at the curbs. A 12" white limit line is drawn across the lanes at each approach. A 5' min. dimension (refer to S-493.0) is shown between the crosswalk and the limit line. At the right end of the segment, a second 12" white limit line is shown. Dimension callouts: '7' max. (see S-490.0 for details)' and '2' max. for uni-directional ramps (see S-490.0 for details)'.

Plan view, intersection, right: A signalized four-leg intersection with an S symbol at the center and continental crosswalks on all four legs (labeled '2' white or yellow, centered on DYCL and lane lines'). A 12" white limit line is on each approach, each set back 5' from the crosswalk (5' dimension shown at the upper right and lower right corners). Curb ramps are shown at each corner. A 'SEE DETAIL' dimension arrow points to the bar spacing.

Detail: Install 2' wide white or yellow markings along striping. Center the markings on DYCL and lane lines. Add markings according to chart below. Marking should be installed such that wheels straddle the crosswalk markings.

Table (lane width and bar spacing on center):
Lane width 9' / spacing 4.5'
Lane width 10' / spacing 5.0'
Lane width 11' / spacing 5.5'
Lane width 12' / spacing 6.0'
notes:
1. Implementation. This standard plan applies to installations in accordance with MPP Section 344 for Continental Crosswalks for new and reinstallations of marked crosswalks on signalized and stop-controlled approaches.
2. Crosswalk width. Typical crosswalk widths are 15 feet but may vary according to site conditions. Continental markings shall be installed within existing dimensions unless otherwise indicated on a signed plan.
3. Midblock crosswalks. This standard plan also applies at controlled midblock approaches in accordance with S-493.0 - Location of Limit Lines and Crosswalks.
4. Conflict between signed plan and standard plan. Should conflicts arise between this Standard Plan and a signed signal or geometric plan with their associated markings (e.g., "cat tracks," extension of the DYCL, etc.), the signed plan shall take precedent.
5. Retrofitting and resurfacing. Refer to MPP Section 344 for retrofitting and resurfacing.

Detail text: Install 2' wide white or yellow markings along striping. Center the markings on DYCL and lane lines. Add markings according to chart below. Marking should be installed such that wheels straddle the crosswalk markings.
title: Continental Crosswalks on Controlled Approaches
summary: Shows continental (ladder) crosswalk markings for new and reinstalled marked crosswalks on signalized and stop-controlled approaches, per MPP Section 344. Bars are 2 ft wide, white or yellow, centered on the DYCL and lane lines, and spaced 4.5 ft, 5.0 ft, 5.5 ft and 6.0 ft on center for 9 ft, 10 ft, 11 ft and 12 ft lanes so wheels straddle the bars. A 12 in. white limit line is set 5 ft minimum from the crosswalk and a signed plan takes precedence over this standard.

description:
Layout on Two-Lane Street: Plan view of a two-lane street with a centerline (CL), shown with break lines, curb returns at the right end and the roadway width marked VARIES. Two asphalt speed humps (Type I or Type II) are drawn as shaded bands across the full roadway width, each 12' or 22' long along the street, with Type I chevron markings shown on each hump (see Sheet 4 for Type II). A reflective white thermoplastic HUMPS pavement legend is placed in each approach lane ahead of the first hump. Signs W17-1 and W13-1(15) are placed at each end of the layout, 100' to 250' (+/-) before the nearest hump (marked with asterisk, see Note 5). The spacing between the two humps is 250' to 600' (+/-). Section cut A-A is marked across the right-hand hump, looking at the gutter edge.

Layout on Street with Striped Median: The same layout on a street with a striped median (double centerline with two lane lines shown dashed), with the same 12' or 22' hump length, 100' to 250' (+/-) from the sign to the first hump, 250' to 600' (+/-) between humps, W17-1 and W13-1(15) signs at each approach (see Note 5), HUMPS legends ahead of each hump, Type I or Type II asphalt hump, and Type I marking shown (see Sheet 4 for Type II). Section A-A is marked across the right-hand hump.

Section A-A: A cross section at the curb. From the curb face, the hump edge is set back a width that varies (marked with asterisk), then a 12" taper runs up from the gutter to full A.C. (asphalt concrete) thickness, labeled 'A.C. Standard 3/8" Aggregate Mix'. Footnote: '* If there is no actual gutter use 2' from flow line.' The curb and gutter are shown as a stippled concrete section.
notes:
This sheet has no numbered notes block. Notes printed on the views:
* See Note 5 (sign and hump spacing; Note 5 is on Sheet 2 of 4).
Type I marking shown. See Sheet 4 for Type II.
Section A-A: A.C. Standard 3/8" Aggregate Mix. Width * varies. 12" taper. Curb face. * If there is no actual gutter use 2' from flow line.
Reflective white thermoplastic pavement markings (HUMPS legend).
Dimensions: 12' or 22' hump length. 100' to 250' (+/-) sign to hump. 250' to 600' (+/-) between humps.
title: Speed Humps (Sheet 1 of 4: Layouts and Section A-A)
summary: Standard details for Type I (12 ft long) and Type II (22 ft long) asphalt speed humps, their chevron markings, and the advance warning sign and HUMPS pavement legend. Sheet 1 shows sign and hump placement on two-lane streets and on streets with a striped median, with signs W17-1 and W13-1(15) 100 ft to 250 ft ahead of the first hump and 250 ft to 600 ft between humps. Section A-A shows the 12 in. taper and the 3/8 in. aggregate A.C. mix at the gutter.

description:
Advance Warning Sign: Elevation of a sign post at the curb with a SPEED HUMPS diamond sign above a square 15 MPH plate. The diamond is labeled '30" X 30" W17-1 Modified with Type II-A Retro-Reflective Sheeting'. The plate is labeled '24" X 24" W13-1(15) with Type II-A Retro-Reflective Sheeting'. The post is labeled 'Sign post'. A horizontal dimension of 12" min. is shown from the curb face line to the sign edge. A vertical dimension of 7' min. runs from the sidewalk surface up to the bottom of the plate. The curb face is labeled.

Advance Pavement Marking (See S-509.0): Plan view of the pavement legend HUMPS drawn in large outlined letters reading upward in the lane. The lane width W runs from the geometric or striped centerline (or solid yellow line of a striped median) on the left to the curb face or flow line on the right. The legend is offset from the centerline by 2' if W>10' and 1' if W=10'.

Speed Humps Installation Notes: Seven notes listed below.
notes:
Advance warning sign callouts: 30" x 30" W17-1 modified with Type II-A retro-reflective sheeting. 24" x 24" W13-1(15) with Type II-A retro-reflective sheeting. 12" min. from curb face. 7' min. mounting height. Sign post.
Advance pavement marking callouts: Geometric or striped centerline or solid yellow line of striped median. Curb face or flow line. W. Offset by 2' if W>10', 1' if W=10'.

Speed Humps Installation Notes
1. Speed humps shall be installed only when authorized by LADOT. Installations shall conform to the latest revision of LADOT Specification No. 51-008-003.
2. All asphalt concrete pavement shall conform to the most recent edition of the Standard Specification for Public Works Construction Section 302-5.
3. Speed humps shall not be placed over maintenance covers, watergates, junction chambers, etc.
4. Edge of speed humps should be 5 ft. or more from edge of driveway or catch basin.
5. Spacing between humps may vary. Exact locations and type of speed humps and sign locations shall be determined by LADOT.
6. Asphalt joins shall be accomplished by feather-edging.
7. The height of the speed hump shall not be less than 2 5/8 inch, and shall not exceed a tolerance of +1/4 inch.
title: Speed Humps (Sheet 2 of 4: Advance Warning Sign, Pavement Marking and Installation Notes)
summary: Standard details for Type I (12 ft long) and Type II (22 ft long) asphalt speed humps, their chevron markings, and the advance warning sign and HUMPS pavement legend. Sheet 2 gives the advance warning sign (30 in. x 30 in. W17-1 modified over a 24 in. x 24 in. W13-1(15) plate, 7 ft minimum mounting height, 12 in. minimum from curb face), the HUMPS pavement legend offset 2 ft if W is over 10 ft or 1 ft if W is 10 ft (see S-509.0), and seven installation notes.

description:
Type I Speed Hump Marking (Chevron I): Plan view of a Type I hump, 12' long along the street (vertical in the drawing) across a driving lane W on each side of the centerline (CL), with the gutter at the outer edges. At the top, typical dimensions show an 8' total chevron width made up of 1', 1.5', 3', 1.5', 1' segments, with the whole marking offset from the centerline by 2' if W>10' and 1' if W=10'. Each side of the centerline carries a pair of white chevrons: on the left a V shape, and on the right an inverted V (pointing up) with a smaller nested chevron inside it. The hump is shaded. Along the left edge dimensions show the 12' hump length and 4.5' from the flow line, with the flow line and edge of gutter labeled. A 12" taper is marked at each gutter edge, and section marks A and A (labeled 'See Page 1') show the Section A-A location at the left gutter. Section cut B-B is marked along the centerline of the hump. The hump spans 'Type I Speed Hump' between the 12" tapers and the driving lane W is dimensioned on each side of CL.

Section B-B: Profile of the Type I Speed Hump, 2 5/8" high by 12' long, with vertical height dimensions at 6" typical spacing from the start of the hump. Starting at 0 at the beginning, the heights are 0.42", 0.80", 1.15", 1.46", 1.73", 1.97", 2.17", 2.34", 2.46", 2.55", 2.61" and 2.62" (2 5/8") at the crest at 6'. The profile then falls back to zero at 12' total length.
notes: Callouts and labels: Typical dimensions. Offset by 2' if W>10', 1' if W=10'. 12" Taper. See Page 1 (Section A-A). Flow line. Edge of gutter. Type I Speed Hump. Driving Lane W. Type I Speed Hump Marking (Chevron I). 6" Typical (spacing of height stations). Type I Speed Hump 2 5/8" High by 12' long, Section B-B.
title: Speed Humps (Sheet 3 of 4: Type I Hump Marking and Section B-B)
summary: Standard details for Type I (12 ft long) and Type II (22 ft long) asphalt speed humps, their chevron markings, and the advance warning sign and HUMPS pavement legend. Sheet 3 shows the Type I (Chevron I) marking, 12 ft long with an 8 ft chevron width built from 1, 1.5, 3, 1.5 and 1 ft segments, offset 2 ft from the centerline if W is over 10 ft or 1 ft if W is 10 ft, and the Section B-B profile with its 2 5/8 in. crest at mid-length.

description:
Type II Speed Hump Marking (Chevron II): Plan view of a Type II hump, 22' long, across a driving lane W on each side of the centerline (CL). At the top, typical dimensions show an 8' chevron width with 1', 1.5', 3', 1.5', 1' segments, and an offset from the centerline of 2' if W>10' and 1' if W=10'. Along the left edge the hump length is dimensioned 6' (Slope), 10' (Flat Top) and 6' (Slope), with the flow line and edge of gutter labeled. The left side of the centerline carries a column of white V-shaped chevrons, and the right side carries a column of inverted V chevrons that point up. On the right edge the chevron zones are dimensioned 12', 12' and 4.5' from the flow line. A 12" taper is marked at each gutter edge. Section marks A and A are labeled 'See Page 1' and section cut C-C is marked along the hump centerline.

Section C-C: Profile of the Type II Speed Hump, 2 5/8" high by 22' long, symmetric about its centerline. Each end ramp is 6' long (6" typical station spacing) rising from 0 to a crest height of 2.62" (2 5/8"), with heights 0.42", 0.80", 1.15", 1.46", 1.73", 1.97", 2.17", 2.34", 2.46", 2.55", 2.61" and 2.62" (2 5/8"). Between the ramps the top is flat at 2.62" (2 5/8"), shown as two 5' segments either side of the centerline, giving a 10' flat top and 22' overall length.
notes: Callouts and labels: Typical dimensions. Offset by 2' if W>10', 1' if W=10'. 12" Taper. See Page 1 (Section A-A). Flow line. Edge of gutter. Type II Speed Hump. Driving Lane W. Type II Speed Hump Marking (Chevron II). 6" Typ. (spacing of height stations). Type II Speed Hump 2 5/8" High by 22' long, Section C-C.
title: Speed Humps (Sheet 4 of 4: Type II Hump Marking and Section C-C)
summary: Standard details for Type I (12 ft long) and Type II (22 ft long) asphalt speed humps, their chevron markings, and the advance warning sign and HUMPS pavement legend. Sheet 4 shows the Type II (Chevron II) marking on a 22 ft long hump, with 6 ft slopes at each end and a 10 ft flat top, the same 8 ft chevron width and centerline offset as Type I, and the Section C-C profile with a 2 5/8 in. crest.

description:
Raised Crosswalk Marking (Chevron III): Plan view across two travel lanes, one on each side of the centerline (CL), each labeled TRAVEL LANE. Reading along the street, the raised crosswalk is divided into a 6' min approach ramp, a 10' min crosswalk (see Note 1) and a 6' min departure ramp. The crosswalk section has three black bars in each travel lane. On the approach ramp each lane carries a chevron (V) marking pointing back toward approaching traffic, and on the departure ramp each lane carries the chevron facing the opposite direction, with a nested inner chevron. The chevron is centered in the lane and is dimensioned across its width as 1', 1.5', 3', 1.5', 1'. The departure chevron is 4.5' tall.

Bicycle Ramp Marking (Chevron IV): Plan view of a bike lane crossing the raised crosswalk. Centered in the lane is a small chevron pointing along the bike lane, with a width of 10", 10", 14", 10", 10" across and a 14" dimension at its top. The bicycle ramp is dimensioned 12.5% MAX. SLOPE and the chevron length 4.5'. Below the ramp is the BIKE LANE and the FLAT TOP of the raised crosswalk with three black crossing bars.

Sidewalk Culvert Markings: Plan view of a street edge with an 8" minimum white edgeline and 3 flexible delineators on the lane line spaced 20' on center, shown as two 20' dimensions (20' TYP and 20'). At the end, a hatched area marks the sidewalk culvert with chevron markings and four crosswalk bars.
notes:
Callouts: Centered in lane. 6' min approach ramp. 10' min crosswalk (see Note 1). 6' min departure ramp. Travel lane. 4.5'. 1', 1.5', 3', 1.5', 1'. Bicycle ramp 12.5% max. slope. Centered in lane 10", 10", 14", 10", 10". 14". 4.5'. Bike lane. Flat top. 8" minimum white edgeline. 3 flexible delineators on lane line spaced 20' on center. 20' TYP. 20'.
Note 1 referenced on this sheet is given on Sheet 3 of 3: the width of the top of raised crosswalks should match the width of the connecting sidewalk, shared use path, or desired crosswalk, but not less than 10' in width.
title: Raised Crosswalks (Sheet 1 of 3: Chevron III, Chevron IV and Sidewalk Culvert Markings)
summary: Standard details for raised crosswalks with bicycle ramps across a bike lane, including approach and departure ramps, Chevron III and Chevron IV markings, and the sign assemblies for advance warning. Sheet 1 shows the Chevron III raised crosswalk marking (6 ft minimum approach ramp, 10 ft minimum crosswalk, 6 ft minimum departure ramp, chevron 1, 1.5, 3, 1.5 and 1 ft wide), the Chevron IV bicycle ramp marking at a 12.5% maximum slope, and sidewalk culvert markings with delineators 20 ft on center.

description:
Raised Crosswalk Marking and Signs: Plan view of a two-lane street with a raised crosswalk and curb ramps at the top and bottom curbs. The raised crosswalk has black and white crosswalk bars with a Chevron III marking in each lane on both sides (labeled 'CHEVRON III MARKING, TYP. SEE STANDARD DETAIL'). Humps (shaded ramp areas) are shown at the curb ramps. Crosswalk sign assemblies are placed at the crosswalk on each curb. On each approach an advance sign assembly (see Note 2) is placed at distance C** upstream of the crosswalk, and a HUMPS 'ADVANCED WARNING PAVEMENT MARKING, SEE STANDARD DETAIL S-509.0, SEE NOTE 2' is placed in the lane near the advance sign. Break lines show the street continuing between the sign location and the crosswalk.

Crosswalk Assembly (elevation): Four stacked signs: W11-2 (pedestrian diamond), W17-1bP (RAISED CROSSWALK plaque), W16-7P (diagonal arrow plaque), and W13-1 (15 MPH advisory speed plaque).

Advance Assembly (elevation): Four stacked signs: W11-15 (bicycle and pedestrian diamond), W17-1bP (RAISED CROSSWALK plaque), W16-9P (AHEAD plaque), and W13-1 (15 MPH).

Advisory Speed Plaques: W13-1 (15 MPH) with asterisk, W13-1 (20 MPH), W13-1 (25 MPH), W13-1 (30 MPH). *As appropriate for raised crosswalk design speed.
notes:
Callouts: Chevron III marking, typ. See standard detail. Curb ramp. Crosswalk sign assembly. Advance sign assembly, see Note 2. Advanced warning pavement marking, see standard detail S-509.0, see Note 2. C**.
Sign assemblies: Crosswalk assembly: W11-2, W17-1bP (RAISED CROSSWALK), W16-7P, W13-1 *. Advance assembly: W11-15, W17-1bP (RAISED CROSSWALK), W16-9P (AHEAD), W13-1 *.
Advisory speed plaques: *W13-1 (15 MPH), W13-1 (20 MPH), W13-1 (25 MPH), W13-1 (30 MPH).
* As appropriate for raised crosswalk design speed.
Note 2 referenced on this sheet is given on Sheet 3 of 3: the placement of advanced warning signs and markings shall follow the guidance for advanced sign posting (C**) shown on S-481.0.
title: Raised Crosswalks (Sheet 2 of 3: Markings and Signs)
summary: Standard details for raised crosswalks with bicycle ramps across a bike lane, including approach and departure ramps, Chevron III and Chevron IV markings, and the sign assemblies for advance warning. Sheet 2 shows the raised crosswalk plan with Chevron III markings, curb ramps, crosswalk and advance sign assemblies at distance C**, and the advance HUMPS pavement marking per S-509.0. It also gives the sign stacks: crosswalk assembly W11-2, W17-1bP, W16-7P and W13-1, advance assembly W11-15, W17-1bP, W16-9P and W13-1, with advisory speeds of 15, 20, 25 or 30 MPH.

description:
Raised Side Street Crosswalk, Standard Curb Ramp (upper plan): Plan view of a side street crossing at a corner, with a bike lane running along the side street in a shaded green strip (optional solid green colored pavement) with a bicycle symbol and a 10' dimension along the lane. The bike lane approaches the crossing and ends with a Chevron IV bicycle ramp marking (see Sheet 1), a bicycle crossing marking with three bars, and a bicycle yield line with triangle (shark teeth) marks. A curb ramp and sidewalk are shown at the corner. Across the side street, a raised side street crosswalk has 24" white crosswalk bars, with a Raised Crosswalk Marking (Chevron III) at its edge. A limit line (if needed) is shown 2' wide near the stop location on the cross street. The bicycle crossing marking is also labeled.

Raised Side Street Crosswalk, Depressed Corner (lower plan): The same arrangement at a depressed corner. The bike lane in optional solid green colored pavement approaches from the bottom with a direction arrow and 10' dimension, a bicycle yield line, a Chevron IV bicycle ramp marking, and a 12" white crosswalk marking (the bike crossing bars). The raised side street crosswalk has 24" white crosswalk bars with a Chevron III marking (see Sheet 1), the bicycle crossing marking is labeled, and the sidewalk is shown at the corner.
notes:
NOTES
1. The width of the top of raised crosswalks should match the width of the connecting sidewalk, shared use path, or desired crosswalk, but not less than 10' in width.
2. The placement of advanced warning signs and markings shall follow the guidance for advanced sign posting (C**) shown on S-481.0.
3. See City of Los Angeles Supplemental Street Design Guide, Detail 600 for raised crossing details.

View callouts: Optional solid green colored pavement. Bicycle ramp marking (Chevron IV), see Sheet 1. Curb ramp. Limit line (if needed). Sidewalk. 24" white crosswalk. 12" white crosswalk. 2'. 10'. Bicycle yield line. Bicycle crossing marking. Raised crosswalk marking (Chevron III), see Sheet 1.
title: Raised Crosswalks (Sheet 3 of 3: Raised Side Street Crosswalk at Standard Curb Ramp and Depressed Corner)
summary: Standard details for raised crosswalks with bicycle ramps across a bike lane, including approach and departure ramps, Chevron III and Chevron IV markings, and the sign assemblies for advance warning. Sheet 3 shows a raised side street crosswalk at a standard curb ramp and at a depressed corner, both with a bike lane in optional solid green pavement, a Chevron IV bicycle ramp marking, a bicycle yield line and bicycle crossing marking, and 24 in. white crosswalk bars. Three notes cover the 10 ft minimum top width, advance sign placement per S-481.0 and Supplemental Street Design Guide Detail 600.

description:
Typical Signs and Lane Reduction Markings - Reference MUTCD Section 3B.09 and Figure 3B-12(CA): Plan view of a multilane roadway with a curb lane that ends. W9-1 is placed at distance d upstream of the taper, W4-2 is placed at d/4 (marked 'See Table 1' for d), and the lane drop arrows are spaced d/2 apart. At the end an 8" white line forms the taper (see Table 1) with 12" W diagonals, leading into a hatched area labeled 'Parking lane or narrowed roadway'. Dimensions shown are d, d/4, d/2 and d/2, and a 2' dimension appears at the taper.

Peak period lane to all day parking lane: Plan of the curb lane with a lane line. A 3-7PM MON-FRI plate (see note 1) is attached to the W9-1 and W4-2 signs. Before the taper the curb is marked 'Tow Away No Stopping (Peak hours only)', and beyond the taper 'All day parking permitted'. An 8" white line taper (see table 1) with 12" W diagonals leads to an 8' parking lane (7' minimum) with parked cars at the curb line.

Full time lane to peak period lane: Plan of the curb lane with a lane line. An EXCEPT 3-7PM MON-FRI plate (see note 2) is attached to the W9-1 and W4-2 signs. The curb is marked 'Tow Away No Stopping Any Time' before the taper and 'Tow Away No Stopping (Peak hours only)' beyond it, with parked cars shown at the curb line at right.

Table 1:
Columns: posted speed limit (mph) / posted speed limit plus 5 mph / "d" distance (feet) / d/4 (feet) / taper rate (minimum)
25 / 30 / 450 / 113 / 15:1
30 / 35 / 550 / 138 / 20.5:1
35 / 40 / 650 / 163 / 26.7:1
40 / 45 / 750 / 188 / 45:1
45 / 50 / 850 / 213 / 50:1
50 / 55 / 950 / 238 / 55:1
55 / 60 / 1100 / 275 / 60:1

Signs: W4-2 (diamond sign showing a lane ending) and W9-1 (diamond sign reading RIGHT LANE ENDS).
notes:
Table 1 footnote: "d" = Advance Placement Distance per MUTCD, section 2C.05, Condition A. Taper rates and "d" distances shown are based on posted speed plus 5 mph. Where the 85% speed (critical speed) on the approach is determined to be equal or less than the posted speed, the table numbers for the next lower speed increment may be used.

Notes:
1. Where the lane dropped is a peak period lane, the W9-1 and W4-2 signs shall be modified by the addition of a black-on-yellow sign plate below to indicate the hours during which the curb lane is used by moving traffic.
2. Where the lane drop is installed in advance of a parking lane which is used as a thru lane for peak period traffic, the W9-1 and W4-2 signs shall be modified by the addition of a black-on-yellow sign plate below to indicate the excepted hours during which the lane is continuous.

View labels: Typical Signs and Lane Reduction Markings - Reference MUTCD Section 3B.09 and Figure 3B-12(CA). Taper (see Table 1). 8" white line. 12" W diagonals. Lane line. Curb line. Parking lane or narrowed roadway. 8' parking lane (7' minimum). Tow Away No Stopping (Peak hours only). All day parking permitted. Tow Away No Stopping Any Time. 3-7PM MON-FRI plate (see note 1). EXCEPT 3-7PM MON-FRI plate (see note 2).
title: Lane Reduction
summary: Typical signs and pavement markings for a lane reduction (lane drop), based on MUTCD Section 3B.09 and Figure 3B-12(CA). It shows the permanent lane drop and two peak-period cases, a peak-period lane that becomes an all-day parking lane and a full-time lane that becomes a peak-period lane. Table 1 gives the advance placement distance d, d/4 and the minimum taper rate by posted speed (using posted speed plus 5 mph), for example 450 ft and 15:1 for a 25 mph road. W9-1 and W4-2 signs are used, with a black-on-yellow plate when the lane is peak-period only.

description:
Plan view: A signalized four-leg intersection (S symbol at the center) with exclusive bus lanes along the curb on each approach. On each approach the curb lane carries BUS ONLY legends (the words ONLY and BUS in tall letters reading along the lane) and bus lanes are delineated by 8" solid lines labeled '8" (See Note 5)'. At the left (west) approach, a left turn pocket with a closed entrance and an arrow is shown with the legend ONLY BUS next to the turn arrow. The bottom approach shows a bus turn lane with a left turn arrow, ONLY, and BUS, with a curving lane line. Opposing lanes show normal lane lines and a double centerline.

Typical Spacings (shown twice, once at the upper left approach and once at the right approach): each detail shows a straight arrow, the legend ONLY and the legend BUS placed in a row along the lane, with dimensions 18' (arrow), 16', 8', 8', 8' and an overall 16', as drawn. On the left approach the order from upstream to the stop line is arrow, ONLY, BUS with dimensions 18', 16', 8', 8', 8' and 16'. On the right approach the order is mirrored with dimensions 8', 18', 16', 8', 8' and 16'.
notes:
Notes:
1. These pavement markings are supplementary to signing which regulates use of the exclusive bus lanes.
2. Install the "BUS ONLY" pavement markings at the beginning of bus turn lanes and at the beginning and ending of each block where there is a bus only curb lane.
3. Bus only turn lanes shall be supplemented with turn pavement arrows.
4. Contra-flow bus only lanes shall be supplemented with straight ahead direction pavement arrows.
5. Concurrent-flow bus only lanes shall be delineated by 8" solid white lines. For a part-time bus lane installation, which is used as a mixed flow lane during non-restricted hours, a 4" solid white line shall be used.
6. Bus only left turn pocket lanes shall have a closed entrance delineated by the extension of the 8" white barrier line.
7. Mid-block pavement markings for bus only curb lanes shall be installed where the block length exceeds 700 feet.
8. The "BUS ONLY" pavement markings shall conform to the 8' high Caltrans standard.
9. All markings shall be Alkyd-Based thermoplastic.

Callouts: Typical spacings. 8" (See Note 5).
title: Exclusive Bus Lane Pavement Markings
summary: Typical BUS ONLY pavement markings for exclusive bus lanes, shown at a signalized intersection with legends and arrows on the approaches and at bus turn lanes. Typical spacings of 18 ft for the arrow and 16 ft and 8 ft for the legend words are dimensioned. Markings are installed at the start of bus turn lanes, at the start and end of each block with a bus only curb lane, and mid-block where the block exceeds 700 ft. Concurrent-flow lanes are delineated by 8 in. solid white lines, or 4 in. for part-time lanes, and all markings are alkyd-based thermoplastic.

description:
Case 1: Bi-directional ramps: Plan view of a street corner with a curved curb (CURB RADIUS shown from the radius point to the curb, with M.C. and 'CL typically near M.C.' marking the ramp centerline near the middle of the curve). One bi-directional curb ramp is drawn at the corner on the curve. The curb ends at ECR (end of curb return) on the west leg and BCR (beginning of curb return) on the north leg. A marked CROSSWALK crosses each leg, with the crosswalk edge lines. Point C is the crosswalk corner nearest the ramp. Dimensions A and B are shown at the crosswalk offset near the corner: A is measured from the crosswalk line to the curb line prolongation, and B is measured from the crosswalk edge to the curb line prolongation.

Case 2: Uni-directional ramps: Plan view of a similar corner with two uni-directional curb ramps, one at each end of the curve (one on each leg near ECR and BCR). Point C is the crosswalk corner, with a 2' MAX. dimension from the crosswalk to the curb line prolongation. The crosswalk on each leg is dimensioned CROSSWALK. Lane lines, a double yellow centerline and curbs are shown.

No notes are printed on this sheet. It is sheet 1 of 2.
notes: No numbered notes appear on this sheet. Labels: Case 1: Bi-directional ramps. Case 2: Uni-directional ramps. CURB. ECR. BCR. Curb radius. M.C. CL typically near M.C. Crosswalk. A. B. C. 2' MAX.
title: Crosswalk Alignment (Sheet 1 of 2)
summary: Guidance for aligning marked crosswalks relative to curb ramps at intersection corners. Case 1 covers bi-directional ramps and uses offset dimensions A, B and C, and Case 2 covers uni-directional ramps with a 2 ft maximum offset. No notes appear on this sheet, and the limits for A, B and C are referenced from S-481.1 and S-490.0 elsewhere.

description:
Plan view: A vertical street shown at four successive intersections with a freeway interchange at the bottom. At the top, the first intersection shows lane markings with 'SEE NOTE 1' and 'SEE NOTE 3' callouts at the pavement arrows. Below, two blocks are dimensioned 250'~650' each (between intersections) with Elephant Tracks (short dashed lane drop markings) across the intersections. W4-7 is placed near the start of the first trap section and W73A(CA) is placed in advance of the second, with 'SEE NOTE 2' at the elephant tracking. At the lower end, R3-7 is placed at an intersection near the freeway, with 'SEE NOTE 3' at the arrows, and the right turn lane is terminated by a curved barrier line with hatching, separated from the through lane by a longitudinal line. 'SEE NOTE 6' is shown at the lower signalized (S) intersection and the freeway ramps (labeled 'Freeway') are drawn with direction arrows. At the bottom, another intersection shows 'SEE NOTE 1' and 'SEE NOTE 3' at its arrows.

Signs: W73A(CA) (RIGHT LANE TURNS RIGHT AHEAD, diamond sign), W4-7 (THRU TRAFFIC MERGE LEFT, diamond sign), R3-7 (RIGHT LANE MUST TURN RIGHT, rectangular sign).
notes:
Notes:
1. The second (downstream) pavement marking is not mandatory if advance turn lane is 100' long or less. At locations where a right turn is prohibited at an intermediate intersection during limited hours, the pavement arrow at that intersection should be deleted.
2. Continuous through lanes that terminate as mandatory turn lanes and that are not otherwise regulated by the Vehicle Code, (commonly known as "Trap Lanes") shall be delineated by Elephant Tracks. The length of Elephant Tracking should be two blocks in advance of the mandatory turn, but not less than 500 feet and not more than 1,300 feet. This striping shall be supplemented with W4-7 and W73A(CA) signing. The W4-7 sign should be placed near the start of the Elephant Tracks.
3. Added turn lanes (i.e. having no continuity upstream) traversing through all intervening intersections shall be delineated by Elephant Tracking (lane drop markings) and pavement arrows as shown.
4. Trap Lanes should be considered where it is not feasible to drop a lane with the standard signing and pavement markings. They should terminate at arterial streets or freeway ramps.
5. Trapped lanes for left turns should have overhead signing.
6. Trapped lanes for right turns shall be terminated by a curved barrier line and separated from the adjacent through lane by a longitudinal line. Barrier lines for right-turn lanes should be 100' minimum.
7. Placement of arrows should also conform with Standard Plan S-456.0.

Sign labels: W73A(CA), W4-7, R3-7. Dimensions: 250'~650' between intersections.
title: Advance Turn Lanes
summary: Marking and signing for advance (added) turn lanes and trap lanes, where a through lane ends as a mandatory turn lane. Trap lanes are delineated by elephant tracks, starting about two blocks ahead of the turn but not less than 500 ft and not more than 1,300 ft, with 250 ft to 650 ft shown between intersections. They are supplemented with W4-7 and W73A(CA) signs and an R3-7 sign. Right-turn trap lanes end with a curved barrier line at least 100 ft long, and left-turn trap lanes need overhead signing.
